complaint: When I open a trace for an SMS message I only ever see the first two services. Where does the rest of it go?

response.restated_complaint: When viewing a trace for an SMS message, only the first two services (comms-ingest, comms-orchestrator) show up, and the engineer wants to know where the rest of the journey (comms-sender, provider) is going.

hypotheses.summary: This is an SMS-only trace-context bug, not a message-loss bug: all 8 of 8 accepted SMS messages actually complete (delivered=8, lost=0), but at the hop where comms-sender consumes from the channel queue, the consumer starts a brand-new root trace instead of continuing the producer's trace context. So the trace ID you're looking at literally ends at comms-orchestrator's publish — the second half of the journey exists but lives under a different trace ID. Email (0/29 broken) and push (0/4 broken) don't show this, which localises the bug to the SMS-handling path in comms-sender's consumer, and there are no message-scoped logs for SMS to bridge the gap either — only correlation_id ties the two trace halves together.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: Directly matches the complaint's channel (SMS) and symptom (trace stops after two services) with observed confidence and a channel-by-channel contrast that rules out the hop itself as the cause.

hypotheses.summary: A broader, channel-agnostic detector sees the same symptom at the same node: of 40 traversals of comms-orchestrator's publish -> comms-sender's consume, 8 break into a new trace while 32 link correctly, and every other hop in the pipeline propagates context fine. This is consistent with (and likely the same root cause as) the SMS-specific finding, but is computed independently across all channels rather than being scoped to SMS by name.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: Same underlying symptom from a different, higher-severity detector; included because it's a distinct finding_id that corroborates the localisation to the comms-sender consumer rather than the queue/transport.

ruled_out.claim: The rest of the message is being lost/dropped, not just untraceable.
ruled_out.why_not: SMS channel shows delivered=8, lost=0 in the pipeline summary, and D4's evidence confirms all 8 SMS messages reach the end — the break is in trace propagation, not in message delivery.

ruled_out.claim: The queue/transport hop itself is dropping the trace context for everyone.
ruled_out.why_not: context_intact_elsewhere shows every other hop, including the one immediately after the broken one (consume -> send), propagates context correctly, and other channels (email, push) show 0 breaks on this exact hop.

would_resolve: The context-extraction code in the comms-sender consumer for SMS, compared against the channel that works (per D4's would_resolve)

Whether other message types besides SMS also appear among the 8 broken traversals in the broader INV.context_break finding, to confirm it is entirely SMS-driven or partially overlapping with another channel
